card.name: Spots just before a speaker is named
card.fires_on: Punctuation or word endings right before a quoted speaker or spokesperson is named or referred to, such as a closing quote comma before "said Dr. X", or a possessive after a person's name. Most often in news-style quotes.

modes.label: Closing quote before attribution
modes.description: A comma or exclamation inside the closing quote mark, just before the speaker tag like "she recalled" or "said Chang".
modes.example: Determining how to optimize outcomes with the smallest cost to the quality of life is a treatment decision every radiation oncologist faces<<,">> said Chang.

modes.label: After a person's name
modes.description: A possessive or name part right after a named person, in news text about what that person said or did.
modes.example: A photo taken Monday captures Vice President Joe Biden<<'s>> response to a Milwaukee second-grader's

card.writes: It suppresses words like representative, spokesperson and members, so it lowers the chance of a generic group or spokesperson word coming next.
card.plain: It fires where a quote ends and a named speaker is about to be introduced, and it discourages words like "spokesperson" there.
